ai_show_review.summary: Soaring Dark Star, blistering Good Lovin' and tight high‑energy flow
ai_show_review.blurb: The Pirates World show delivers a soaring Dark Star, a blistering Good Lovin' jam and a fiery High Time→Dark Star→The Other One sequence. Jerry’s guitar is on fire while the rhythm section drives a festival‑energy momentum throughout. The Miller soundboard capture is crisp, well‑balanced and essentially complete.
ai_show_review.review: On March 24, 1970 at Pirates World in Dania, FL, the Dead unleashed an electric set that still feels fresh today. Opening with a concise Morning Dew, they quickly built into a powerhouse of Good Lovin' – where Bob Weir’s lead shines – and a tight, soulful rendition of Don't Ease Me In. The centerpiece is a soaring Dark Star that showcases Jerry’s “on‑fire” leads and Phil’s bass that sounds like a whole new instrument, followed by an exhilarating High Time→Dark Star→The Other One segue that keeps the band in constant motion. A brief but fiery Cold Rain And Snow adds a touch of Americana before the set closes with a tight Drums‑Not Fade Away‑Turn On Your Lovelight medley and a classic Me And My Uncle. The Miller SBD (gd70-03-24.sbd.miller.32054.sbeok.flacf) captures every nuance – crisp highs, tight lows, and only a single splice at 5:02 of Dark Star – making this the definitive listening source for an already legendary performance.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard capture with crisp, well‑balanced audio and only a minor splice; it presents the full energy of the show with minimal noise.

key_highlights: Dark Star soaring with urgent guitar and deep bass support.
High Time→Dark Star→The Other One seamless segues delivering high‑energy momentum.
Good Lovin' jam featuring Weir’s standout leads and jazzy drum breaks.
Excellent Miller soundboard: crisp highs, tight lows, virtually complete performance.

band_performance.Jerry: Garcia delivers fiery, soulful leads throughout – dueling with Bob on Morning Dew, soaring on Dark Star and driving the High Time→Dark Star transition with emotive vocals.
band_performance.Phil: Lesh provides deep rhythmic support, sounding like a different instrument during the Dark Star jam and anchoring the high‑energy flow of the set.
band_performance.Bob: Weir’s rhythm work is solid, highlighted by dueling guitar on Morning Dew and a standout lead during Good Lovin' and Cold Rain And Snow.
band_performance.Mickey: Hart contributes locomotive power and creative fills, especially in the jazzy drum build‑up into Good Lovin'.
band_performance.Billy: Kreutzmann delivers machine‑gun precision with an appropriately placed solo and strong breaks that keep the momentum driving forward.
